source.body:
**Bug Description**

Moving a variable into a scope that already has a variable with the same key succeeds and creates a duplicate key. `PATCH /variables/:id` only validates key uniqueness when the request changes the `key` field, so a move request that only sends `projectId` skips the check. Neither the database nor the entity model enforces uniqueness on `(key, project)`, so two variables with the same key end up in one scope.

Creating a variable with a duplicate key and renaming one into a taken key are both rejected by the service — the move is the only path that reaches this state. Once a scope holds two variables with the same key, `$vars` resolution for that scope becomes order-dependent (the resolver lets the later row overwrite the earlier one), so workflows read a value that depends on database/cache ordering.

**To Reproduce**

1. Instance with the variables feature licensed. Create a variable with key `SHARED_KEY` (value `1`) in project A.
2. Create another variable with key `SHARED_KEY` (value `2`) in project B (different projects, so this is allowed).
3. Send `PATCH /variables/:id-of-project-A-variable` with body `{"projectId": "<project B id>"}` — note there is no `key` field in the body.
4. The request succeeds. Project B now shows two variables with key `SHARED_KEY`.
5. Run a workflow in project B that reads `{{ $vars.SHARED_KEY }}` — whether it resolves to `1` or `2` depends on row order, not on anything the user configured.

**Expected behavior**

The move should be rejected with the same error the create and key-change paths produce, e.g. `A variable with key "SHARED_KEY" already exists in the specified project` (and the equivalent message when moving to global). When the update moves and renames at the same time, the new key is the one that should be validated.

**Debug Info**

```
n8nVersion: 2.49.0 (source build, master @ 75fe21cb)
database: sqlite
n8n_executions_mode: main
consumerId: n/a (local source build)
```

The behavior is server-side logic and is not specific to this environment.

## Environment

**Operating System:** Windows 11 (affects all platforms; the issue is in the variables service, not platform-specific)

**n8n Version:** master @ 75fe21cb (2026-11-22), still present on current master (bf31087b)

**Node.js Version:** 24.20.0

**Database:** SQLite (default)

**Execution mode:** main (default)

**Hosting:** self hosted

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: I checked the current `variables.service.ee.ts`: `update()` computes the destination project, but calls `validateUniqueVariable()` only inside `if (variable.key)`. A PATCH with only `projectId` therefore skips the duplicate check even when moving into a scope with the same key, which matches this report. The check needs to use the effective key (`variable.key ?? existingVariable.key`) when the key or scope changes, while excluding the current variable ID.
